items.title: HSV en Hajduk Split bezorgen Vuskovic onvergetelijke rentree na dopingstraf
items.summary: Mario Vuskovic mag zich na een dopingschorsing van vier jaar weer voetballer noemen. De HSV-verdediger maakte zondag zijn rentree tegen zijn oude liefde Hajduk Split in een oefenduel dat volledig in het teken stond van zijn terugkeer op het veld. De Kroaat deed ruim een uur mee en werd door een nagenoeg vol Volksparkstadion in het zonnetje gezet.

items.title: Record-breaking Andy Robertson is Scotland’s finest captain
items.summary: As he passes Kenny Dalglish’s appearance total, it is important to remember that it is the left-back’s journey that sets him apart Andy Robertson may not be Scotland’s greatest player, but he is indisputably their finest captain. It counts as sacrilege, even to generations who have watched Kenny Dalglish only on YouTube, to reputationally place Robertson above the Liverpool hero on the basis of a cap haul that will reach 103 in St Gallen on Monday. Dalglish’s international career ended at 102 and the curious events that meant he missed the 1986 World Cup. There is no requirement to compare a left-back in 2026 to a forward from decades earlier. Dalglish and Robertson are men in different positions in essentially a different sport. Instead, Robertson’s march to the top of the cap pile gives cause to laud his contribution. Continue reading...

items.title: Terry Butcher: ‘I’ve learned to live with the Hand of God goal better’
items.summary: The former England centre-back answers your questions on Diego Maradona, Bobby Robson and on staying in strange places “Have you made up all these on your own?” asks Terry Butcher, sitting in a London office in the week he is presented with his England legacy cap. It turns out dozens of Guardian readers want to pick the brains of a much-loved centre-back who was feted en route to a World Cup semi-final and tormented four years previously by the mercurial genius of Diego Maradona. Did Maradona ever admit to the “Hand of God”? Butcher found himself in the post-match doping-control room alongside his nemesis at the Azteca in 1986. “I tapped my head, then my hand, and then he tapped his head,” Butcher says. “He didn’t admit to it because, if he had, I’d have been right across that room.” Continue reading...

items.title: Declan Rice accepts he had an ‘average World Cup’ as England gear up for Spain showdown
items.summary: Midfielder needed a break ‘to come back stronger’ James Trafford selected to start in goal for England Declan Rice has admitted he had an “average” World Cup at the end of a gruelling season and needed time out during the international window in September and October in order to return stronger. The Arsenal midfielder believes the break has served its purpose, having produced starring performances against Bayern Munich and Liverpool in recent weeks. He is now ready to hit his best level for England in Sunday’s Nations League showdown against Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium. Continue reading...

items.title: De la Fuente adamant there is no racism in Spain despite England reminder to players
items.summary: De la Fuente tells Tuchel ‘we’re not racists, none of us’ Tuchel hits out at media for ‘creating confusion’ Luis de la Fuente has told Thomas Tuchel there is no racism in Spain after the England coach’s admission that he would remind his players of the anti-racism protocol prior to their meeting at the Metropolitano on Sunday night. This will be the first time the countries play each other in Madrid since some of England’s black players were subjected to racist abuse in a match at the Santiago Bernabéu in 2004. And although England have returned to Spain three times without incident since then, twice in Seville and once in Alicante, Tuchel was asked on Friday about going back in the buildup to Sunday’s game. The England coach replied that England “will not expect anything [untoward]” but also said: “Maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Madrid].” Continue reading...
